questions.question: What is a structure? Name and describe the three kinds of structures, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A structure is anything with a shape that can support a load. A solid structure is solid all the way through, like a brick wall. A shell structure is hollow with a strong outer covering, like an egg. A frame structure is strong parts joined together with spaces between, like a pylon or ladder.

questions.question: Why are frame structures useful? What shape makes them stiff?
questions.expected_answer: They are strong but light, because they use less material and have empty space between the parts. Triangles make them stiff, because a triangle cannot be pushed out of shape.

questions.question: Explain why a vertebrate skeleton is a frame structure.
questions.expected_answer: It is made of strong bones, the members, joined at joints, with muscles and skin covering it, like walls covering a building's frame. The frame carries the load of the body and gives it shape.
